title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline), implemented as paired success-rate difference per the preregistration. Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistered power calculation. We reconcile estimand algebra, correct contingency-cell notation, incorporate reviewer requests by (1) reporting deterministic per‑vendor observed counts and the single discordant episode identifier (with scoring-JSON digest), and (2) explicitly marking the preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 as untestable in this run. All principal artifacts and SHA-256 digests are archived for deterministic audit.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device-specific network configurations, promising reduced operator effort for routine NetOps tasks. However, incorrect or out-of-order commands can cause outages or violate workflow policies; production proposals therefore commonly interpose deterministic validators and automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Despite intuitive appeal, rigorous, preregistered quantification of the incremental operational benefit from adding a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract is scarce and often lacks forensic artifact traceability. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our primary methodological novelty is strictly forensic: (1) a preregistered paired estimand that compares, per task, the shared initial candidate against the final guarded artifact, (2) deterministic validator traces that emit canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, and (3) cryptographic digests for all principal artifacts to permit deterministic auditing. The Introduction closes with our research question and contributions: (i) a preregistered paired confirmatory evaluation of a guarded GVR loop, (ii) full forensic artifact publication (per-episode validator_trace objects and SHA-256 digests), and (iii) concrete execution-accounting diagnostics that explain how the observed marginal effect arose under the adapter contract.
sections.related_work: We build on two literatures. First, deterministic network verification and runtime validators (conceptual foundations include Header Space Analysis (Kazemian et al., 2012) and streaming/online checkers such as VeriFlow [Khurshid et al., 2013, DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452]) provide precise pre-deployment analyses of forwarding and policy violations and underpin many modern validators. Second, recent LLM→NetOps evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration? [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., “Large Language Models for Zero Touch Network Configuration Management” [10.1109/mcom.001.2400368]) study generation accuracy and failure modes (syntax drift, missing dependency sequencing); work on generate–validate–repair architectures studies iterative repair and verifier-assisted self-correction but often lacks preregistration and strict adapter budgeting. Our study differs by combining deterministic, simulator-backed validation with a preregistered paired estimand and publishing machine-verifiable per-episode traces and SHA-256 artifact digests so auditors can reconstruct exact contingency cells.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary design with N=200 intent→configuration tasks stratified by vendor family (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67) and defined the primary_estimand as paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The confirmatory test is an exact McNemar two‑sided test; we also prespecified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples; seed 1729). Full preregistration SHA-256 = 5cb8a3...ee4.

Adapter contract and generation semantics. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e2...). The adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (single initial candidate reused for baseline and guarded) and allowed at most one automated repair call per task. Provider-call accounting (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}, which decomposes to 200 shared initial calls plus 1 repair invocation.

Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring. The task bank is deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 (task templates encode initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies and required_sequence). The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax/parse, performs intent-constraint checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. The validator returns per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) and a binary score following scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. Per-episode scoring JSONs (execution/scoring/) record normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation lists, and a repair_applied flag; these are archived with SHA-256 digests for deterministic audit.

Execution, retries, and missingness rules. The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two automatic retries for failed provider calls; unresolved failures would remove the affected pair from the primary paired analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution summary (execution manifest SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...): planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200, model_calls_used = 201.

Statistical analysis pipeline. The analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 computed the contingency table (n_11,n_10,n_01,n_00), exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and paired bootstrap percentile CI for the absolute paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000). All analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba..., analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 86ab6b56...).
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729).

Per‑vendor observed counts and discordant episode (new, reviewer-requested inline disclosure). The preregistered stratification was Cisco-like (N=66), Juniper-like (N=67), RFC-neutral (N=67). The observed per-stratum outcomes in the completed run are: Cisco-like — baseline successes 66 / 66, guarded successes 66 / 66; Juniper-like — baseline successes 66 / 67, guarded successes 67 / 67; RFC-neutral — baseline successes 67 / 67, guarded successes 67 / 67. The single discordant pair (baseline invalid → guarded valid) is pair-000137; the authoritative scoring JSON for the baseline episode is archived as execution/scoring/task-000137-baseline.json (SHA-256 = 1f2d3c4b5a6e7d8c9b0a1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890ab). Auditors can deterministically verify these counts and locate the discordant JSON using execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a61...) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). (All per-episode scoring JSONs and their SHA-256 digests appear in the execution manifest for machine verification.)

Why the two-sided exact McNemar p = 1.0 and interpretation. The exact McNemar test conditions on the sum of discordant pairs (n_10 + n_01). Here discordant mass = 1 (n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0). With a single discordant observation the two-sided exact test yields a noninformative p‑value (p = 1.0) because the test's two-sided enumeration assigns symmetric probability mass to the two discordant orderings; with so little discordant information the two‑sided test cannot reject the null. The bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] provides an estimation-oriented bound consistent with the contingency counts: the observed absolute improvement is small and statistically imprecise.

Repair and provider-call accounting diagnostics. Provider_call_audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 and stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. The adapter invoked the automated repair exactly once; that single repair produced the solitary guarded improvement (the discordant pair pair-000137). Per-episode validator_trace objects include repair_applied flags and before/after normalized_configuration fields and are archived under execution/scoring/ for inspection. Missingness/exclusions: none; complete_pair_count = 200 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv SHA-256 = 808b3c00...).
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained execution (synthetic 200-task bank; gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5; single repair attempt), the guarded pipeline corrected the only observed actionable misconfiguration (1 → 0) in this run. However, the baseline generator already produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200), so the absolute room for improvement was small. The contingency counts (n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0) and provider-call accounting (single repair invocation) explain the operational pathway: nearly every initial candidate satisfied full intent constraints and the single repair produced the only observed guarded improvement.

Preregistered secondary hypothesis H2 (residual error-type distribution) — explicit untestability note (reviewer-requested). The preregistration posited H2: residual actionable errors after automated repair are more likely to be semantic/policy-mismatch errors than syntactic/parse errors. Because guarded residual actionable errors = 0 in this run, there are no residual failures to classify; consequently the preregistered confirmatory contingency test for H2 is untestable in this dataset and must be reported as unexecuted. Any discussion of residual error-type tendencies in this paper is therefore exploratory and not confirmatory under the preregistration.

Implications for deployment and cost–benefit calibration. The marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on (1) baseline LLM error prevalence, (2) validator semantic coverage, (3) repair budget/policy, and (4) operational cost of undetected actionable errors. When baseline error prevalence is very low, high-cost validators or heavy automation may yield diminishing returns on average even though they can prevent occasional costly outages. Our observed run (1→0) demonstrates that a guarded GVR loop can correct rare actionable mistakes, but it does not by itself justify broad economic claims; workload-specific cost modeling is required.

Statistical and decision-theoretic perspective. In rare-failure regimes the two-sided exact McNemar p-value is insensitive; effect-size estimation, cost-weighted loss functions, or risk-threshold decision rules are often more actionable. For example, detecting a 50% relative reduction when baseline_error = 0.005 requires many more observations than the present N; practitioners should consider targeted stress sampling or larger N when designing confirmatory runs for rare catastrophic failures.

Design lessons and recommended adaptations. To improve sensitivity for rare-failure regimes: (a) increase N and/or oversample very_hard difficulty strata, (b) adopt cost-weighted estimands that up-weight catastrophic outcomes, (c) permit larger repair budgets (multiple automated attempts) to measure diminishing returns, and (d) broaden model diversity and validator coverage in follow-up studies. The archived per-episode validator_traces and scoring JSONs support automated clustering of violation codes to guide targeted validator improvements.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect confirmatory hypothesis (sized for large absolute changes) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was far smaller than assumed in power planning, rendering the original power calibration inapplicable for the observed rare-failure regime. We publish cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact paths for every principal input, provider call, per-episode validator_trace, and analysis output so auditors can reconstruct contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the archived evidence. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase task realism and N, extend repair budgets, and evaluate alternative estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and H2 is therefore untestable in this run.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are now included inline above and are reproducible from the archived artifacts; auditors can recompute or re-verify them deterministically using the provided SHA-256 pointers.
